messages.author: 57ddef5748efce88
messages.subject: simmer problem definition (de)serializer
parts:
Over time simmer has become a more and more mature DES framework (much thanks to Iñaki).

I currently use simmer mostly in an ad-hoc analysis kind of way: simulating a current system and formulating an advise on it. However, I would like to start using it in a more dynamic way, e.g. integrating it into a website front-end or in existing IT systems. To easily achieve this I think a (de)serializer is the way to go. Another advantage is also that it will become easy to share problem definitions (e.g. for educational purposes).

I'm currently thinking of defining the problem definition in a JSON structure.

Here are two examples: https://gist.github.com/Bart6114/0924637a5cf823e54c360c0f54504731 and https://gist.github.com/Bart6114/08bee48bd9e57639aa5ab889a9f8d2c8. The first one is a simple example, the second one contains a more complex branching trajectory. A value encapsulated with "%" will be transformed to a function (if it doesn't evaluate to a function). A value encapsulated with "$" will be evaluated as R code.

I currently have some code up and running for deserialisation (I'll put it up on GitHub), but not yet for serialisation; will have to look into whether every required can be easily accessed.

What do you guys think about the proposed JSON structure? Any other ideas about the (de)serialization?

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] simmer problem definition (de)serializer
parts:
It would be a nice feature indeed. Deserialisation is more or less straightforward, and your proposed JSON structure seems natural to me and easy to use. We may find some clues on this issue in the jsonlite and RJSONIO packages.

The problem comes with serialisation of certain arguments. For instance, once you’ve called at(0, 0, 0), you lose the information about the caller and (which is more important) about the values, and all you have is the returned function, which is:

> at(0,0,0)
function() {
    if (i < length(time_diffs)) {
      i <<- i+1
      return(time_diffs[i])
    } else {
      return(-1)
    }
  }
<environment: 0x3eaadc8>

As you can see, the values are masked into the time_diffs variable. :-\

Iñaki

​

messages.author: 57ddef5748efce88
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] simmer problem definition (de)serializer
parts:
I've been fondling the idea of building a small web interface on top of simmer for demonstration purposes.
What it boils down to however is the difficulty of talking from a language/framework/tool to R and in turn to simmer. There are some adhoc solutions (think of e.g. rpy2), but they are IMO quite adhoc and I try to refrain from using them in production. A "package" that translate a JSON object (something that can be easily constructed in almost every language) into a ready-to-go simmer environment could be useful for these purposes. 

To make it a bit more concrete: for the small web interface I'm talking about I would e.g. build the front-end using AngularJS, create a small HTTP backend in R using jug (https://github.com/Bart6114/jug - heavily biased here :) ) which can work with the simmer.json package. In the front-end you can then construct a problem definition in a visual way, the AngularJS controller translates it into a JSON object, does a POST request using the definition object, the jug instance receives the JSON and calls simmer.json::deserialise(JSON), runs the simulation and returns the result.
